purpose: Audit whether the shared envelope and evidence kernel can support a non-document code patch surface without executing code or adding a new core abstraction.

activities.label: adapt synthetic code events through the shared CloudEvents kernel
attack code identity provenance permission patch base and execution boundaries
record whether the third surface requires a new core abstraction

queries.expression: does the code surface use the shared CloudEvents kernel while adding only patch-specific semantics
does replay across three delivery permutations preserve the same canonical code event order
does the patch oracle verify source state base hash preview permission and no code execution
are external writes and unknown source or workspace conditions blocked

assumptions: The code host and editor workspace are synthetic and local.
The shared CloudEvents kernel handles envelope identity, time and provenance fields.
Patch-specific semantics require a base hash and an independent source check.
Preview is allowed only as a reversible dry-run requiring confirmation.
This audit must not execute or write code.
kill_tests: Missing required code event blocks the adapter.
Mismatched source surface blocks the adapter.
Missing claim provenance blocks the adapter.
Enabling code execution blocks the adapter.
Enabling workspace write blocks the adapter.
Missing preview permission blocks the oracle.
Stale source precondition blocks the action.
A failed source check cannot be presented as passed.
An unknown patch base hash blocks the preview.
unknowns: Whether a real CODE-INE adapter needs syntax-tree anchors beyond the synthetic patch contract.
Whether a production workspace needs a separate sandbox or signing policy.
Whether media surfaces require timeline or codec-specific semantics that do not fit this kernel.
Whether an actual repository API can provide the same independent postconditions.
